newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA SET TO DRAW LEVEL IN SERIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA SET TO DRAW LEVEL IN SERIES.

text.p: Australia were poised to draw level in the Ashes series after reducing England to 130 for five on the fourth day of the third test on Sunday.
With his team chasing a massive target of 469 to win, coach David Lloyd admitted that England faced a huge task to rescue the match and stop Australia drawing level to 1-1 in the series.
"We're alive and kicking but only just. So far, we've been thoroughly outplayed," he said.
Even the English weather, which has been poor in recent weeks, is unlikely to play any part in saving the hosts. The local forecast for Monday is "dry and warm".
England lost their first four wickets in the second innings in a spell of 37 balls either side of tea. Only John Crawley, playing for his place after a poor run, resisted with an unbeaten 53.
Australia had earlier declared their second innings at 395 for eight, Steve Waugh becoming the first batsman for 50 years to make two centuries in an Ashes encounter.
Australia's leg-spinner Shane Warne is determined that his team should level the six-match series at one-each before he flies home on Tuesday for a week to see his wife and new baby.
Warne took six wickets for 48 in England's first innings to tilt the balance of the match in Australia's favour.
On Sunday he weighed in with 53 runs with the bat before taking two wickets as England struggled.
The only enjoyable period of the day for the England fans came during an opening partnership of 44 between Michael Atherton and Mark Butcher.

But England lost Atherton and Alec Stewart in successive overs just before tea. When Jason Gillespie picked off Nasser Hussain and Butcher, four wickets had gone for 11 runs and the Australian victory was in sight.
Warne, having claimed Stewart as his 250th test victim, added Graham Thorpe who made seven.
